question: Do admitted dataset, checkpoint, evaluation and export identities remain bound to the exact bytes consumed, and do invalid artifacts stay unavailable?
hypothesis: Single-read artifact snapshots and registry/evidence admission checks prevent substitution and false availability without changing model objectives or preserved results.
falsifiers: An evaluation, baseline or quantization report names bytes other than the checkpoint it consumed.
Missing, changed or incompatible quantized weights can pass artifact admission.
A caller can substitute a registered dataset, omit a passing held-out evaluation, or relabel the bigram runtime as a reserved model.
A corrupt or unsupported checkpoint is shown as available or produces a response.
A rejected export destroys an existing destination or predecessor evidence.

workflow.data: Fresh local engineering fixtures plus repository-owned Foundry verification corpus; no protected capability campaign.
workflow.training: Exact character-bigram maximum likelihood, seed 7, smoothing 0.25, prefix fraction 0.8.
workflow.split: Nonoverlapping target transition positions; last training character supplies context only for first held-out target.
workflow.independent_unit: This is a deterministic engineering execution, not an independent scientific sample.
workflow.baseline: Frozen uniform distribution over training alphabet.
workflow.admission: Candidate must strictly improve held-out NLL and perplexity; supported checkpoint format, exact source provenance and passing recorded evaluation are required.
workflow.confirmation: No scientific confirmation stage. Artificial failure injections are engineering regressions.
workflow.outputs: Source/config/data/checkpoint identities, held-out metrics, export, fresh-process API and CLI responses, health/error results, timing/RSS, commands and exit codes.

preserved: All historical model results and prior study records remain unchanged; no Hermes promotion or new capability/efficiency claim.

limitations: Deterministic bigram lifecycle and artificial tensor regressions are not assistant-quality evidence.
Initial bigram registration reconstructs training counts/recomputes metrics; serving validates artifact identity and recorded evidence without refitting historical entries.
Deep reports are checked for structural and numerical consistency, not authenticated as measurements by an independent evaluator.
Output freshness is an intentional compatibility change; each deep attempt needs fresh files and a fresh sibling release manifest.
